bill_text.text_with_changes:
A bill for an act relating to state finance; establishing the federal funding protection trust fund; providing for conditional receipt and remittance of federal funds; requiring a report; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes, chapter 16A.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.

[+[16A.5311] MINNESOTA FEDERAL FUNDING PROTECTION TRUST FUND. +]

[+Subdivision 1.+]

[+Purpose and findings.+]

[+(a) The legislature finds that: +]

[+(1) federal funds support critical programs for the health, safety, and welfare of Minnesotans; +]

[+(2) Minnesota relies on predictable, timely, and nondiscriminatory distribution of federal funds appropriated by Congress; +]

[+(3) suspension, delay, or conditional withholding of federal funds for political or nonstatutory reasons creates fiscal instability and undermines cooperative federalism; and +]

[+(4) Minnesota has a compelling interest in protecting residents, local governments, nonprofit providers, and state agencies from disruptions. +]

[+(b) The purpose of this section is to establish a state trust fund mechanism to receive, hold, and manage federal funds and federal pass-through funds in a manner that protects state programs while preserving compliance with federal law. +]

[+Subd. 2.+]

[+Establishment of the trust fund.+]

[+The Minnesota federal funding protection trust fund is established in the state treasury. The trust fund is a special revenue fund and is not part of the general fund. Money in the trust fund is held in trust and may be expended only as provided in this section. +]

[+Subd. 3.+]

[+Sources of funds.+]

[+The trust fund consists of: +]

[+(1) federal funds awarded, granted, or otherwise made available to the state of Minnesota or its agencies; +]

[+(2) federal pass-through funds intended for political subdivisions, nonprofit organizations, or service providers within Minnesota; +]

[+(3) interest earnings on amounts held in the trust fund; and +]

[+(4) any other money authorized by law to be credited to the fund. +]

[+Subd. 4.+]

[+Conditional holding authority.+]

[+(a) Notwithstanding any other law, the commissioner of management and budget, in consultation with the attorney general and the governor, may temporarily hold federal funds in the trust fund if the governor determines that: +]

[+(1) federal funds have been suspended, delayed, reduced, or conditioned in a manner not expressly authorized by federal statute or regulation; or +]

[+(2) federal actions create a material risk of interruption to essential state services. +]

[+(b) Funds held under this subdivision remain dedicated to the original federal purpose and may not be repurposed, transferred, or spent for any other use. +]

[+Subd. 5.+]

[+Release and remittance of funds.+]

[+(a) Federal funds held in the trust fund must be released and distributed when the governor certifies in writing that: +]

[+(1) the federal government has restored or confirmed the availability of funds consistent with federal law; or +]

[+(2) continued holding of the funds would place the state or recipients at risk of noncompliance with federal requirements. +]

[+(b) Certification under this subdivision must be transmitted to the chairs and ranking minority members of the legislative committees with jurisdiction over state government finance and the affected program areas. +]

[+Subd. 6.+]

[+Taxpayer and recipient protections.+]

[+(a) Nothing in this section authorizes the state to: +]

[+(1) collect federal taxes on behalf of the United States; +]

[+(2) interfere with individual or business tax obligations to the federal government; or +]

[+(3) assume liability for federal penalties, interest, or enforcement actions. +]

[+(b) This section must be administered to ensure that individual taxpayers, service recipients, and program beneficiaries experience no disruption in eligibility, benefits, or services to the maximum extent permitted by law. +]

[+Subd. 7.+]

[+Reporting and oversight.+]

[+(a) The commissioner of management and budget must submit a quarterly report to the legislature that includes the: +]

[+(1) amount of federal funds held in the trust fund; +]

[+(2) programs and agencies affected; +]

[+(3) legal or administrative basis for holding the funds; and +]

[+(4) communications received from federal agencies related to the funds. The report must be published on the department's website. +]

[+(b) The legislative auditor must conduct a review of the trust fund within two years of enactment and report findings to the chairs and ranking minority members of the legislative committees with jurisdiction over state budget and finance. +]

[+Subd. 8.+]

[+Severability.+]

[+If any provision of this section is held invalid, the invalidity does not affect other provisions or applications of this section that can be given effect without the invalid provision. +]

Sec. 2. [+EFFECTIVE DATE. +]

[+This act is effective the day following final enactment. +]
bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to state finance; establishing the federal funding protection trust fund; providing for conditional receipt and remittance of federal funds; requiring a report; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes, chapter 16A.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.

[16A.5311] MINNESOTA FEDERAL FUNDING PROTECTION TRUST FUND.

Subdivision 1.

Purpose and findings.

(a) The legislature finds that:

(1) federal funds support critical programs for the health, safety, and welfare of Minnesotans;

(2) Minnesota relies on predictable, timely, and nondiscriminatory distribution of federal funds appropriated by Congress;

(3) suspension, delay, or conditional withholding of federal funds for political or nonstatutory reasons creates fiscal instability and undermines cooperative federalism; and

(4) Minnesota has a compelling interest in protecting residents, local governments, nonprofit providers, and state agencies from disruptions.

(b) The purpose of this section is to establish a state trust fund mechanism to receive, hold, and manage federal funds and federal pass-through funds in a manner that protects state programs while preserving compliance with federal law.

Subd. 2.

Establishment of the trust fund.

The Minnesota federal funding protection trust fund is established in the state treasury. The trust fund is a special revenue fund and is not part of the general fund. Money in the trust fund is held in trust and may be expended only as provided in this section.

Subd. 3.

Sources of funds.

The trust fund consists of:

(1) federal funds awarded, granted, or otherwise made available to the state of Minnesota or its agencies;

(2) federal pass-through funds intended for political subdivisions, nonprofit organizations, or service providers within Minnesota;

(3) interest earnings on amounts held in the trust fund; and

(4) any other money authorized by law to be credited to the fund.

Subd. 4.

Conditional holding authority.

(a) Notwithstanding any other law, the commissioner of management and budget, in consultation with the attorney general and the governor, may temporarily hold federal funds in the trust fund if the governor determines that:

(1) federal funds have been suspended, delayed, reduced, or conditioned in a manner not expressly authorized by federal statute or regulation; or

(2) federal actions create a material risk of interruption to essential state services.

(b) Funds held under this subdivision remain dedicated to the original federal purpose and may not be repurposed, transferred, or spent for any other use.

Subd. 5.

Release and remittance of funds.

(a) Federal funds held in the trust fund must be released and distributed when the governor certifies in writing that:

(1) the federal government has restored or confirmed the availability of funds consistent with federal law; or

(2) continued holding of the funds would place the state or recipients at risk of noncompliance with federal requirements.

(b) Certification under this subdivision must be transmitted to the chairs and ranking minority members of the legislative committees with jurisdiction over state government finance and the affected program areas.

Subd. 6.

Taxpayer and recipient protections.

(a) Nothing in this section authorizes the state to:

(1) collect federal taxes on behalf of the United States;

(2) interfere with individual or business tax obligations to the federal government; or

(3) assume liability for federal penalties, interest, or enforcement actions.

(b) This section must be administered to ensure that individual taxpayers, service recipients, and program beneficiaries experience no disruption in eligibility, benefits, or services to the maximum extent permitted by law.

Subd. 7.

Reporting and oversight.

(a) The commissioner of management and budget must submit a quarterly report to the legislature that includes the:

(1) amount of federal funds held in the trust fund;

(2) programs and agencies affected;

(3) legal or administrative basis for holding the funds; and

(4) communications received from federal agencies related to the funds. The report must be published on the department's website.

(b) The legislative auditor must conduct a review of the trust fund within two years of enactment and report findings to the chairs and ranking minority members of the legislative committees with jurisdiction over state budget and finance.

Subd. 8.

Severability.

If any provision of this section is held invalid, the invalidity does not affect other provisions or applications of this section that can be given effect without the invalid provision.

Sec. 2. EFFECTIVE DATE.

This act is effective the day following final enactment.
